# Instant-Voxel

> Instant-Voxel turns 3D models and images into voxel art in the browser, lets you edit the voxels, and exports
> them for MagicaVoxel, Minecraft, game engines or 3D printing. Files stay on your computer; only the optional model
> server, which you run yourself, receives anything.

A C++ kernel compiled to WebAssembly does the voxelising, and three.js reads the model files and draws the result.
The page opens on a small sample island, so the editor and the exports can be tried straight away. It is designed
for a desktop; on a phone, viewing, converting and exporting work.

## What it takes and gives

- Models in: GLB, glTF, OBJ with MTL, FBX, STL, PLY, 3MF and DAE, with textures and vertex colours.
- Images in: pixel art extruded voxel for voxel, a greyscale heightmap as terrain, or a photo turned into a relief
  by an in-browser depth model.
- Voxelising: up to 512 voxels per side, solid or hollow, with an automatic palette, Minecraft blocks or any `.hex`
  palette.
- Editing: paint, erase, add, fill, pick and box tools, with mirroring, undo and a cut-height slider.
- Exports: `.vox` (MagicaVoxel), `.glb` (game engines), `.obj` (Blender), `.stl` (3D printing) and `.schem`
  (Minecraft WorldEdit, FAWE and Litematica).

## Using it

1. Drop a model, an image or a `.vox` file onto the page, or pick files under Source.
2. Set the size and the other Voxelise options.
3. Touch it up with the Edit tools. Press `?` for the keyboard shortcuts.
4. Choose a format under Export and press Download.
